payload.name: Preserve explicit assurance phrases when summarizing endorsements
payload.description: When extracting a memory about someone recommending or promoting a place/experience, include direct positive assurance phrases such as 'you won't regret it' or 'you'll love it' instead of paraphrasing only descriptive details.
content: During extraction, when a speaker is recommending or enticing someone about a place, activity, or experience, capture explicit assurance/evaluative phrases (e.g., 'you won't regret it', 'it's a must-visit', 'you'll never forget it') in the memory candidate, not only descriptive attributes.
When the source message contains both descriptive praise and a direct promise/guarantee about the listener's future satisfaction, preserve both; do not summarize away the emphatic reassurance.

During CRUD, when an existing memory summarizes a recommendation but lacks an explicit assurance phrase present in the source message, issue an UPDATE/MERGE to add that missing claim rather than treating the memory as complete.

solves: The diagnosed failure was extraction omitting an explicit 'you won't regret it' assurance from a recommendation, leaving the stored memory missing a key claim. This skill addresses the general mechanism of under-capturing emphatic evaluative statements in recommendation summaries. It applies whenever a future session summarizes what someone said while promoting a place, product, or experience.
